coding_generation_prompt: You are the numbers-only Coding Meta-Agent for a contextual time-series forecasting harness. You may use only historical values, horizon, frequency, and reusable coding-skill summaries; never use documents, future values, ground-truth evidence, or facts inferred from text. Generate structurally diverse forecasting programs, including robust baselines, frequency-aware seasonal replay, local-level/trend methods, and rolling-origin selectors or ensembles when supported by the history. Avoid cosmetic variants. Each candidate must explain a falsifiable numeric assumption and an observable failure condition. Internal tuning must use only prefixes of history and should emphasize recent holdouts whose horizon is as close as feasible to the requested forecast horizon while retaining enough folds for stability. Penalize catastrophic fold performance and unnecessary complexity, and always include a conservative finite fallback. Every program must define exactly def forecast(history: list[float], horizon: int, frequency: str) -> list[float] and return exactly horizon finite numbers. Allowed imports are numpy, math, statistics, itertools, functools, and collections. Do not access files or networks, use randomness, eval or exec, or hard-code the supplied series. Return exactly one JSON object: {"programs":[{"name":"short_snake_case","description":"when to use it","assumption":"falsifiable numeric statement","failure_condition":"observable failure condition","code":"def forecast(...): ..."}]}
coding_revision_prompt: You are the inner numbers-only Coding Harness Engineer. Inspect historical rolling-holdout scores, their dispersion, execution errors, and historical values. Rewrite the algorithm when useful rather than merely retuning constants. Produce descendants that address a diagnosed failure through a distinct mechanism such as changing the seasonal period, robustifying level estimation, adapting to a recent regime, damping trends, or replacing unstable winner-take-all selection with a conservative ensemble. Compare median performance, recent-fold performance, and worst-fold loss; do not optimize only the mean or the single latest fold. Use no documents, textual context, future labels, or ground-truth evidence. Preserve def forecast(history: list[float], horizon: int, frequency: str) -> list[float], sandbox restrictions, finite output, and exact horizon length. Return exactly one JSON object: {"programs":[{"name":"short_snake_case","description":"when to use it","assumption":"falsifiable numeric assumption and why it addresses the failure","failure_condition":"observable failure condition","code":"def forecast(...): ..."}]}
retrieval_prompt:
You are the Retrieval Agent for contextual time-series forecasting. Your main objective is precision: retrieve documents only when exact quoted text can distinguish a coding assumption or establish a forecast-horizon driver for the same target, entity, location, and time window. Use the supplied historical timestamps and values as a consistency filter: reject documents whose claimed scale, trajectory, timing, entity, or target conflicts with the observed series unless another cited document supplies the missing bridge. Search in two passes. First seek direct evidence supporting or falsifying the leading numerical assumptions. Then seek counterevidence, resolution notices, entity mismatches, and timing details that could make an apparent impact irrelevant. If prior retrieval output is visible, audit its weakest claim and fill a specific missing field. The follow-up response is an authoritative complete snapshot, not a delta: repeat every prior selected document, evidence item, and impact that remains valid, include corrections and new bridge evidence, and omit anything now ruled out. If prior_decision_feedback is visible, resolve the exact requested gap and then report only gaps that still remain.

Before selecting a document, verify: (1) entity and target identity, (2) event timestamp or explicit schedule, (3) relation to the forecast boundary, (4) whether the quote describes the observation mechanism or the latent target process, and (5) whether the stated magnitude applies to the forecasted quantity. Reject documents that merely share keywords, discuss another site or metric, report an event that ended before the horizon, speculate without a source, or lack an exact supporting quote. Prefer a smaller high-precision set over three superficially relevant documents.

A numerical adjustment is eligible only when one or more exact quotes jointly specify the affected target, direction, magnitude, and bounded interval overlapping the future horizon. The direction and both window boundaries must be literal in those quotes; never use a duration, date, or other unrelated number as the magnitude. Translate percentages only when the denominator is the forecast target. Zero-output or shutdown language is not sufficient unless the quote explicitly states that the measured target is zero throughout the applicable interval. Otherwise set adjustment_kind to none and list the missing information. Never infer timestamps, durations, magnitudes, or causal mappings.

Classify mechanism_layer as observation, latent_process, future_driver, regime, or irrelevant. Historical measurement corruption can affect candidate choice but must not be replayed as a future process change. An event ending before the forecast horizon cannot justify an adjustment. Copy every supporting statement verbatim from a named document. Audit apparent counterevidence internally, but if entity, target, time, or history checks rule a document out, do not include it in selected_document_ids, evidence, impacts, or citations. Include contradictory evidence only when it remains genuinely applicable to the same target and forecast horizon. Return exactly one JSON object: {"query":"assumption-focused query including entity target and dates","selected_document_ids":["doc_1"],"evidence":[{"document_id":"doc_1","claim":"narrow claim supported by the quote","exact_quote":"verbatim quote"}],"impacts":[{"source_document_ids":["doc_1"],"mechanism_layer":"observation|latent_process|future_driver|regime|irrelevant","temporal_relation":"historical|overlaps_future|ended_before_future|unknown","direction":"up|down|stable|unknown","permanence":"temporary|permanent|unknown","adjustment_kind":"preserve|multiply|add|none","adjustment_value":null,"start_timestamp":null,"end_timestamp":null,"rationale":"explicit mapping plus eligibility or rejection reason"}],"sufficient":false,"missing_information":["specific unresolved fact"],"used_skill_names":[]}. For multiply, adjustment_value is the signed fractional change; for add, it is target units. Set sufficient true only when the evidence needed for candidate selection or an eligible adjustment is complete. Skills are search advice, never evidence, and their exact applicable names must be reported.
decision_prompt:
You are the conservative Decision Agent for contextual time-series forecasting. Select only among candidates already executed and historically hindcast; never invent values or edit trajectories. Establish the numerical default using robust historical evidence: prefer low median or aggregate hindcast error, but treat small score differences as ties when fold rankings are unstable, and use worst-fold behavior, recency, assumption plausibility, and simplicity as tie-breakers. Do not override a clearly superior historical candidate merely because retrieved text sounds relevant.

Read retrieval_status first; verifier rejections and unresolved missing_information cannot support an override. Audit every cited retrieval claim before using it. It must contain an exact quote, match the forecast target and entity, and have a known temporal relation. Observation-layer evidence may invalidate extrapolation from corrupted observations but cannot be applied as a latent-process multiplier. Events ending before the horizon cannot alter future values. Generic directional statements cannot justify numerical adjustments. Select an evidence-adjusted candidate only if all required documents explicitly establish target identity, magnitude, and a bounded interval overlapping the horizon; reject it if any mapping is inferred or if the adjustment extends beyond the quoted window. Because adjustment errors can dominate modest model differences, prefer the unadjusted parent whenever eligibility is incomplete.

If evidence could materially change the choice but entity, timing, target mapping, or magnitude remains unresolved, set request_more_retrieval true and name the exact missing fact. On a later decision round, reconsider using newly retrieved evidence; otherwise retain the numerical default. Cite only documents actually used. Return exactly one JSON object: {"selected_candidate_id":"candidate_name","supporting_document_ids":["doc_1"],"rationale":"hindcast comparison, evidence audit, and selection reason","request_more_retrieval":false,"used_skill_names":[]}. Skills never override provenance, validation, or adjustment eligibility.

coding_skills.name: minimax_seasonal_ensemble
coding_skills.description: Use when 24-step seasonality is visible but validation accuracy varies sharply across folds.
coding_skills.assumption: Among the last four observable 24-point holdouts, the two seasonal estimators minimizing median sMAPE plus 0.35 times worst-fold sMAPE will retain their relative advantage on the next holdout.
coding_skills.failure_condition: It fails if the next 24 points undergo a regime change not represented in the rolling holdouts or the true period differs from 24.

coding_skills.name: post_break_damped_trend
coding_skills.description: Use after a large recent level break followed by a smooth trend whose increments are shrinking.
coding_skills.code:
def forecast(history: list[float], horizon: int, frequency: str) -> list[float]:
    import math, statistics
    if horizon <= 0:
        return []
    x = [float(v) for v in history if math.isfinite(float(v))]
    if not x:
        return [0.0] * horizon
    if len(x) < 4:
        return [x[-1]] * horizon
    d = [x[i] - x[i-1] for i in range(1, len(x))]
    tail_start = max(0, len(d) - 80)
    td = d[tail_start:]
    med = statistics.median(td)
    mad = statistics.median([abs(v - med) for v in td])
    scale = max(1e-9, 1.4826 * mad)
    candidates = [i for i in range(tail_start, len(d)) if abs(d[i] - med) > 8.0 * scale]
    start = candidates[-1] + 1 if candidates else max(0, len(x) - 40)
    seg = x[start:]
    if len(seg) < 6:
        seg = x[-min(20, len(x)):]
    sd = [seg[i] - seg[i-1] for i in range(1, len(seg))]
    recent = sd[-min(8, len(sd)):]
    slope = statistics.median(recent) if recent else 0.0
    ratios = [sd[i] / sd[i-1] for i in range(1, len(sd)) if sd[i-1] > 1e-9 and sd[i] >= 0.0]
    decay = statistics.median(ratios[-min(12, len(ratios)):]) if ratios else 0.92
    decay = min(0.95, max(0.75, decay))
    level = seg[-1]
    out = []
    for k in range(1, horizon + 1):
        value = level + slope * decay * (1.0 - decay ** k) / (1.0 - decay)
        out.append(value if math.isfinite(value) else level)
    return out
coding_skills.assumption: The largest standardized first difference in the last 80 observations marks a persistent level break, and the median slope over the final 8 points decays by 5% to 25% per step as estimated from post-break increments.
coding_skills.failure_condition: It fails if the detected jump is transient, another level break occurs within the forecast horizon, or recent increments begin accelerating rather than decaying.

coding_skills.name: robust_cycle_trend
coding_skills.description: Use when oscillation remains stable but its cycle-level baseline is rising or falling; it addresses the progressively worse fold scores by extrapolating robust inter-cycle level changes instead of assuming a fixed recent level.
coding_skills.assumption: Among periods 38 through 48, at least one period has a median rolling-holdout SMAPE below 7%, and the median of the last three cycle-level changes differs from the next cycle-level change by at most 3 units.
coding_skills.failure_condition: It fails when no candidate period scores below 7% on recent holdouts, when the cycle-level change reverses sign, or when the selected period changes by more than 3 samples over two cycles.

coding_skills.name: robust_period_bank
coding_skills.description: Use for long daily forecasts when recent values show a stable non-calendar oscillation and occasional level shifts or isolated spikes; it directly addresses unstable fold selection by averaging the three best nearby periods.
coding_skills.code:
def forecast(history: list[float], horizon: int, frequency: str) -> list[float]:
    import math, statistics
    if horizon <= 0:
        return []
    x = []
    for value in history:
        try:
            value = float(value)
            if math.isfinite(value):
                x.append(value)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            pass
    if not x:
        return [0.0] * horizon
    if len(x) < 70:
        level = statistics.median(x[-min(12, len(x)):])
        return [level] * horizon

    y = x[:]
    for i in range(len(x)):
        window = x[max(0, i - 3):min(len(x), i + 4)]
        med = statistics.median(window)
        deviations = [abs(v - med) for v in window]
        mad = statistics.median(deviations)
        local_steps = [abs(window[j] - window[j - 1]) for j in range(1, len(window))]
        scale = max(1e-9, 1.4826 * mad, statistics.median(local_steps) if local_steps else 0.0)
        if abs(x[i] - med) > 6.0 * scale:
            y[i] = med

    n = len(y)
    periods = list(range(35, min(50, n // 3) + 1))
    if not periods:
        periods = list(range(8, max(9, n // 3 + 1)))

    def period_score(p):
        errors = []
        start = max(2 * p, n - 3 * p)
        for t in range(start, n):
            current_level = statistics.median(y[max(0, t - p):t])
            previous = y[max(0, t - 2 * p):t - p]
            previous_level = statistics.median(previous) if previous else current_level
            pred = y[t - p] + current_level - previous_level
            errors.append(200.0 * abs(y[t] - pred) / max(1e-9, abs(y[t]) + abs(pred)))
        return statistics.median(errors) if errors else float('inf')

    ranked = sorted((period_score(p), p) for p in periods)
    selected = ranked[:min(3, len(ranked))]

    def seasonal_path(p):
        target_level = statistics.median(y[-p:])
        templates = {}
        first = max(0, n - 4 * p)
        for i in range(first, n):
            phase = i % p
            block_age = (n - 1 - i) // p
            block_end = n - block_age * p
            block_start = max(0, block_end - p)
            block_level = statistics.median(y[block_start:block_end])
            templates.setdefault(phase, []).append(y[i] + target_level - block_level)
        template = {phase: statistics.median(values) for phase, values in templates.items()}
        fitted_last = template.get((n - 1) % p, y[-1])
        continuity = y[-1] - fitted_last
        path = []
        for k in range(horizon):
            phase = (n + k) % p
            base = template.get(phase, target_level)
            correction = continuity * math.exp(-(k + 1) / max(1.0, 0.35 * p))
            path.append(base + correction)
        return path

    paths = [(score, seasonal_path(p)) for score, p in selected]
    weights = [1.0 / max(1e-6, score) for score, _ in paths]
    total_weight = sum(weights)
    out = []
    for k in range(horizon):
        value = sum(weight * path[k] for weight, (_, path) in zip(weights, paths)) / total_weight
        out.append(value if math.isfinite(value) else y[-1])
    return out
coding_skills.assumption: During the next 120 observations, the dominant period remains between 35 and 50 samples, and the median absolute error of level-adjusted corresponding phases from the last four cycles remains at most 8 units.
coding_skills.failure_condition: It fails if the baseline changes by more than 15% within one cycle, the period drifts by more than 2 samples per cycle, or the oscillation disappears.

coding_skills.name: robust_seasonal_drift
coding_skills.description: Use for seasonal series with gradual level drift and occasional extreme outliers.
coding_skills.code:
def forecast(history: list[float], horizon: int, frequency: str) -> list[float]:
    import math, statistics
    if horizon <= 0:
        return []
    x = [float(v) for v in history if math.isfinite(float(v))]
    if not x:
        return [0.0] * horizon
    f = frequency.lower()
    p = 24 if 'hour' in f else 7 if 'day' in f else 52 if 'week' in f else 12 if 'month' in f else 4 if 'quarter' in f else 1
    if len(x) < max(4, p + 1):
        return [x[-1]] * horizon
    s = sorted(x)
    lo = s[int(0.05 * (len(s) - 1))]
    hi = s[int(0.95 * (len(s) - 1))]
    y = [min(hi, max(lo, v)) for v in x]
    diffs = [(y[i] - y[i-p]) / p for i in range(p, len(y))]
    slope = statistics.median(diffs[-min(len(diffs), 4*p):]) if diffs else 0.0
    spread = max(1e-9, hi - lo)
    slope = min(spread / max(1, p), max(-spread / max(1, p), slope))
    result = []
    for k in range(horizon):
        phase = (len(y) + k) % p
        vals = [y[i] for i in range(len(y)) if i % p == phase][-4:]
        base = statistics.median(vals) if vals else statistics.median(y[-min(len(y), p):])
        drift = slope * (1.0 - 0.92 ** (k + 1)) / 0.08
        value = base + drift
        result.append(value if math.isfinite(value) else y[-1])
    return result
coding_skills.assumption: Observations sharing a calendar phase have stable relative levels, while the underlying level changes slowly.
coding_skills.failure_condition: It should fail when seasonal phase effects disappear or the level changes abruptly after the final observation.

coding_skills.name: rolling_origin_ensemble
coding_skills.description: Use when validation varies sharply across folds, as here (1.31 to 5.62 sMAPE); recent rolling-origin tests select among robust level, seasonal, trend, and analog forecasts for the current regime.
coding_skills.code:
def forecast(history: list[float], horizon: int, frequency: str) -> list[float]:
    import math, statistics
    if horizon <= 0:
        return []
    x = [float(v) for v in history if math.isfinite(float(v))]
    if not x:
        return [0.0] * horizon
    f = frequency.lower()
    p = 24 if 'hour' in f else 7 if 'day' in f else 52 if 'week' in f else 12 if 'month' in f else 4 if 'quarter' in f else 1

    def clip(a):
        if len(a) < 8:
            return a[:]
        z = sorted(a)
        lo = z[int(0.05 * (len(z) - 1))]
        hi = z[int(0.95 * (len(z) - 1))]
        return [min(hi, max(lo, v)) for v in a]

    def make(a, h, kind):
        y = clip(a)
        n = len(y)
        if not y:
            return [0.0] * h
        recent = y[-min(n, max(6, p)):]
        level = statistics.median(recent)
        if kind == 'level':
            return [level] * h
        if kind == 'seasonal' and n >= p:
            out = []
            for k in range(h):
                phase = (n + k) % p
                vals = [y[i] for i in range(max(0, n - 4 * p), n) if i % p == phase]
                out.append(statistics.median(vals) if vals else level)
            return out
        if kind == 'trend':
            w = min(n, max(8, p))
            q = y[-w:]
            half = max(2, w // 2)
            slope = (statistics.median(q[-half:]) - statistics.median(q[:half])) / max(1.0, w - half)
            spread = max(q) - min(q)
            slope = max(-spread / max(4, p), min(spread / max(4, p), slope))
            return [level + slope * (1.0 - 0.85 ** (k + 1)) / 0.15 for k in range(h)]
        if kind == 'analog' and n >= 2 * p + h:
            context = y[-p:]
            cm = statistics.median(context)
            scale = statistics.median([abs(v - cm) for v in context]) or 1.0
            matches = []
            for end in range(p, n - h):
                old = y[end-p:end]
                om = statistics.median(old)
                dist = sum(abs((context[j] - cm) - (old[j] - om)) for j in range(p)) / (p * scale)
                matches.append((dist, end, om))
            matches.sort()
            chosen = matches[:min(5, len(matches))]
            if chosen:
                return [level + statistics.median([y[end + k] - om for _, end, om in chosen]) for k in range(h)]
        return [level] * h

    kinds = ['level', 'seasonal', 'trend', 'analog']
    scores = {k: [] for k in kinds}
    block = min(24, max(4, horizon))
    first = max(12, p + 1)
    origins = list(range(first, len(x) - block + 1, block))[-6:]
    for origin in origins:
        actual = x[origin:origin + block]
        for kind in kinds:
            pred = make(x[:origin], block, kind)
            err = [200.0 * abs(a - b) / max(1e-9, abs(a) + abs(b)) for a, b in zip(actual, pred)]
            scores[kind].append(statistics.median(err))
    ranked = sorted(kinds, key=lambda k: statistics.median(scores[k]) if scores[k] else (0.0 if k == 'level' else 1e9))
    selected = ranked[:2]
    paths = [make(x, horizon, k) for k in selected]
    out = [sum(path[i] for path in paths) / len(paths) for i in range(horizon)]
    return [v if math.isfinite(v) else x[-1] for v in out]
coding_skills.assumption: The candidate with the lowest median sMAPE over at least three recent 24-step pseudo-holdouts will score within 1.0 sMAPE point of the best candidate on the next 24 observations; this addresses the parent's unstable fold ranking by reselecting locally.
coding_skills.failure_condition: It fails when the next 24 observations enter a regime absent from recent pseudo-holdouts or all candidate models have rolling median sMAPE above 8.

coding_skills.name: signed_acceleration_trend
coding_skills.description: Use on smooth monotone tails where the parent incorrectly dampens an accelerating negative slope; it estimates signed acceleration directly from recent increments.
coding_skills.code:
def forecast(history: list[float], horizon: int, frequency: str) -> list[float]:
    import math, statistics
    if horizon <= 0:
        return []
    x = []
    for v in history:
        try:
            z = float(v)
            if math.isfinite(z):
                x.append(z)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            pass
    if not x:
        return [0.0] * horizon
    if len(x) < 4:
        return [x[-1]] * horizon
    d = [x[i] - x[i - 1] for i in range(1, len(x))]
    w = min(48, len(d))
    y = d[-w:]
    mt = 0.5 * (w - 1)
    my = sum(y) / w
    den = sum((i - mt) ** 2 for i in range(w))
    accel = sum((i - mt) * (y[i] - my) for i in range(w)) / den if den else 0.0
    slope = my + accel * (w - 1 - mt)
    robust_slope = statistics.median(y[-min(9, w):])
    slope = 0.6 * slope + 0.4 * robust_slope
    accel_cap = 0.5 * max(abs(slope), 1e-9) / w
    accel = max(-accel_cap, min(accel_cap, accel))
    nonnegative = min(x) >= 0.0
    level = x[-1]
    out = []
    for k in range(1, horizon + 1):
        step = slope + accel * k
        level += step
        if nonnegative and level < 0.0:
            level = 0.0
        out.append(level if math.isfinite(level) else out[-1] if out else x[-1])
    return out
coding_skills.assumption: Over the next 50 samples, first differences remain approximately linear in time, with fitted acceleration bounded to at most 0.5 times the current slope magnitude over the fitting window.
coding_skills.failure_condition: It fails if the median absolute residual of the fitted recent differences exceeds 25% of the current slope magnitude, or if a level break occurs during the horizon.

retrieval_skills.name: boundary_regime_transition
retrieval_skills.description: Identify operational changes at the forecast cutoff that can cause an immediate and sustained shift from the preceding local regime.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When occupancy, operating mode, equipment activation, staffing, or another structural condition may change at or near the forecast boundary.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Search for cutoff-adjacent evidence of the prior regime ending, the new regime beginning, the mechanisms activated by that transition, and whether routine operations make the resulting effect persistent.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Accept a regime-change claim only when reliable evidence establishes the transition timing relative to the cutoff, identifies a plausible causal mechanism, and supports persistence over the forecast horizon; preserve exact quotations, provenance, and temporal-window constraints where required.

retrieval_skills.name: bounded_disruption_retrieval
retrieval_skills.description: Search for explicitly bounded operational disruptions within the forecast window and connect verified latent-process constraints to the observable series without extrapolating beyond the documented interval.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When a forecast may be affected by temporary outages, shortages, closures, policy shifts, or other regime changes during a defined horizon.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Search using the process type, disruption synonyms, and forecast-window bounds; prioritize sources that state both the start and end of the event and explicitly describe its effect on the measured outcome.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Accept an adjustment only when evidence places the disruption inside the forecast window, bounds its duration, and directly supports the claimed impact on the observable series; preserve exact quotes and provenance when required, and do not extend the effect outside the verified interval.

retrieval_skills.name: bounded_event_regime_retrieval
retrieval_skills.description: Search for documented operational events within the forecast window, then translate verified start, duration, and recovery statements into latent-process and regime claims without extending beyond the evidence.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When a forecast may be affected by a discrete outage, lockout, shutdown, recovery, or other externally documented regime change.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Combine the event type, affected process or location, and forecast-window bounds; seek sources that independently establish onset, operational impact, duration, and recovery behavior.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Accept a claim only when the evidence directly supports the affected process, temporal overlap, and regime effect; preserve exact-quote and provenance requirements, and do not infer unreported timing, duration, magnitude, or recovery shape.

retrieval_skills.name: bounded_outage_retrieval
retrieval_skills.description: Retrieve evidence that distinguishes a temporary observation-system outage from a genuine change in the underlying process and identifies the outage boundaries and recovery condition.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When a forecast window may overlap maintenance, disabled sensing, telemetry interruption, or another recording artifact.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Search using the sensor or series identifier, measurement type, outage or maintenance terms, and the forecast-window bounds; extract claims about capture behavior, recorded-value behavior, interval boundaries, and restoration of service.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Apply an outage claim only when reliable evidence explicitly covers the target measurement and forecast interval, supports the asserted recorded-value behavior, and bounds the effect or states recovery; preserve exact quotations and provenance when required, and do not infer physical-system values from missing or disabled telemetry.

retrieval_skills.name: incident_regime_recovery
retrieval_skills.description: Retrieve evidence that connects an observed telemetry anomaly to a documented remediation and subsequent return to baseline, separating observation, future-driver, and regime-change claims.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When forecasting an operational metric affected by a known incident, overlapping data corruption, or remediation near the forecast boundary.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Search for incident reports, deployment records, and telemetry summaries covering the forecast boundary and horizon; identify overlapping corruption windows, remediation timing, stabilization behavior, and baseline restoration without treating corrupted measurements as genuine system behavior.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Accept claims only when authoritative, attributable evidence places the event within the required temporal window and explicitly supports the remediation-to-recovery sequence; preserve exact-quote and provenance requirements, cross-check timestamps, and reject inferred recovery or baseline restoration not directly evidenced.

retrieval_skills.name: layered_event_anomaly_retrieval
retrieval_skills.description: Retrieve and separate evidence about real-world demand drivers, operational stress, and measurement-system anomalies that can jointly explain an unusual observed series.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When forecasting around a known event window where physical conditions, public activity, infrastructure operations, or reporting changes may affect either the underlying signal or its observation.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Search the target window using combinations of location, measured quantity, disruption terms, relevant external events, and instrumentation changes. Classify each supported claim as a causal driver, system response, or observation artifact, and preserve uncertainty when a source describes magnitude without locating it precisely in time.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Accept a claim only when a source directly supports the event, mechanism, and relevant temporal relationship. Do not assign an untimestamped magnitude to a specific interval, conflate reporting artifacts with real demand changes, or relax quotation and provenance requirements.

retrieval_skills.name: mechanism_layered_event_verification
retrieval_skills.description: Retrieve horizon-specific evidence by separately establishing the external driver, its causal effect on the latent process, and the validity of the observed signal.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When a forecast horizon may be affected by a bounded event and the resulting observation could be mistaken for measurement error.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Search for sources that explicitly overlap the forecast window, then gather claims for three layers: the future driver, the mechanism linking it to the target process, and an observation-level confirmation that the signal is genuine. Preserve exact temporal bounds, provenance, and quoted quantities during extraction.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Apply an adjustment only when authoritative evidence explicitly covers the forecast window, identifies the direction and magnitude or bounded effect, explains the causal mechanism, and distinguishes real process change from telemetry or reporting failure.

retrieval_skills.name: mechanism_linked_event_retrieval
retrieval_skills.description: Retrieve evidence that connects an external driver through the affected process to the observed metric, while preserving explicit provenance, temporal alignment, and exact quantitative wording.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When a forecast-window event may explain an observed or expected change and the claim requires both causal context and a verified measurement.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Search using the location or system type, target metric, event category, and precise forecast window; then collect evidence separately for the external driver, the intermediate mechanism, and the recorded observation, prioritizing sources that explicitly state the magnitude and time interval.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Accept a quantitative impact only when a reliable source explicitly gives the magnitude, metric, and matching temporal window; verify that the driver, mechanism, and observation refer to the same incident, and reject inferred or merely qualitative magnitudes.

retrieval_skills.name: regime_aware_driver_retrieval
retrieval_skills.description: Retrieve evidence that separates operational regime changes, measurement artifacts, latent process trends, and future drivers before forecasting.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When historical observations may reflect shutdowns, sensor inactivity, policy changes, or a changing underlying trend that could invalidate simple persistence.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Search for authoritative material covering the forecast window and the immediately relevant history; query separately for operating schedules or suspensions, telemetry semantics during inactivity, sustained process trends, and announced future conditions. Convert findings into distinct regime, latent-process, and future-driver claims.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Accept each claim only when its source provenance is clear, its wording supports the claim without inference beyond the evidence, and its effective period overlaps or materially informs the forecast window. Distinguish missing or inactive telemetry from genuine zero values, preserve exact quotations when required, and reject stale, ambiguous, or temporally mismatched evidence.

retrieval_skills.name: window_aligned_mechanism_retrieval
retrieval_skills.description: Retrieve operational evidence that identifies a causal mechanism affecting the forecast target within the forecast horizon, then translate it into a narrowly bounded target constraint.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When public records may document outages, supply failures, closures, or other latent processes that directly alter the target during a defined forecast window.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Search using the affected system or category, the forecast-window boundaries, the suspected operational mechanism, and target-linked outcome terms; prioritize records that jointly establish the event duration, mechanism, and observed target impact.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Accept a claim only when reliable evidence aligns the event with the forecast window and explicitly supports both the causal mechanism and the target outcome; preserve exact temporal bounds, provenance, and quote fidelity, and do not extrapolate beyond the documented interval.

retrieval_skills.name: windowed_dynamics_verification
retrieval_skills.description: Retrieve evidence that directly connects the latest observed motion pattern to its documented continuation within the forecast window while rejecting unsupported quotations and impact claims.
retrieval_skills.applicability: When forecasting a telemetry series whose recent trend may persist, slow, reverse, or terminate during a defined future window.
retrieval_skills.query_strategy: Search for source material combining the system behavior, recent telemetry anomalies, forecast-window boundaries, and documented continuation or deceleration; prioritize passages that explicitly bridge observations to the forecast interval.
retrieval_skills.verification_rule: Accept a claim only when a traceable source explicitly supports both the stated dynamic behavior and its relevance to the forecast window; reject ungrounded quotes, missing provenance, and inferred impacts without verified citations.

decision_skills.name: bounded_evidence_override
decision_skills.description: Override a baseline forecast only over the interval where verified future evidence directly determines the observation process, while retaining the baseline elsewhere.
decision_skills.applicability: When temporally aligned evidence establishes a deterministic, localized recording effect during part of the forecast horizon.
decision_skills.decision_rule: Prefer the evidence-adjusted candidate when verified evidence directly specifies observed values or capture behavior within explicit bounds; mutate predictions only inside those bounds, treat the effect as observational unless evidence supports a physical change, and preserve the validated baseline outside the affected interval.
decision_skills.failure_condition: Do not use this rule when the evidence is unverified, ambiguous about the measured series, outside the forecast window, missing clear temporal bounds, silent about recorded values, or describes the underlying process rather than the observation mechanism.

decision_skills.name: bounded_trend_extrapolation
decision_skills.description: Extrapolate recent first differences with a simple time-varying trend while constraining acceleration so the forecast cannot depart implausibly fast from the observed slope.
decision_skills.applicability: When recent observations show a smooth, persistent directional trend and competing seasonal or break-based models have weaker empirical support.
decision_skills.decision_rule: Fit a local trend to recent first differences, extend it through the horizon, and impose a conservative bound on acceleration relative to the magnitude of the observed slope; select this model when diagnostics support continuity and no verified structural break dominates.
decision_skills.failure_condition: Do not use when recent differences are unstable, a persistent level break or recurring phase pattern is well supported, the bound is arbitrary relative to observed dynamics, or extrapolation violates known physical or domain constraints.

decision_skills.name: validated_cycle_persistence
decision_skills.description: Prefer a phase-aligned seasonal forecast when recent cycles show a stable dominant period and level-adjusted corresponding phases remain consistently accurate.
decision_skills.applicability: When a time series exhibits repeated cycles and recent phase analogs can be evaluated directly.
decision_skills.decision_rule: Select the phase-aligned seasonal candidate only if the dominant period remains stable across recent windows and the robust error of level-adjusted corresponding phases stays below a predeclared tolerance.
decision_skills.failure_condition: Do not use when periodicity is unstable, too few cycles are observed, phase errors exceed tolerance, or a structural break invalidates recent-cycle analogs.

decision_skills.name: verified_event_override
decision_skills.description: Override phase-aligned or historical extrapolation only when verified forward-looking evidence specifies a temporally bounded intervention with a defensible signed effect.
decision_skills.applicability: When normal seasonal assumptions conflict with strong evidence of an exceptional event occurring within the forecast horizon.
decision_skills.decision_rule: Select the evidence-adjusted candidate when the event-window overlap, causal direction, effect interpretation, and observation validity are all verified; restrict the adjustment to the supported interval and translate multiplicative evidence into a signed fractional change without extending it beyond the source.
decision_skills.failure_condition: Do not use when evidence is retrospective, outside the horizon, weakly sourced, causally ambiguous, missing observation-validity checks, or insufficiently precise about timing or effect size.

decision_skills.name: verified_future_override
decision_skills.description: Override a persistence baseline when verified forward-looking evidence establishes a concrete, time-bounded change in the forecast target.
decision_skills.applicability: When reliable evidence describes a future driver that directly affects the target within the forecast horizon and its direction, magnitude, and active window can be mapped to the forecast.
decision_skills.decision_rule: Prefer the evidence-adjusted candidate over the fallback, applying the documented impact only during its supported window and retaining the baseline elsewhere.
decision_skills.failure_condition: Do not use when the evidence is unverified, merely contemporaneous, outside the forecast window, unrelated to the target, ambiguous about timing or direction, or based only on an observation anomaly rather than a true target change.
